items.briefing:
Cybersecurity researchers are warning that AI is now being actively used by criminals to make cyberattacks faster and harder to detect. Separately, a new report shows ransomware attacks have jumped 40% — with many incidents going unreported publicly, meaning the real threat may be larger than it appears. Both trends are relevant to Australian organisations of all sizes, including training providers who hold sensitive student and staff data.

To reduce your risk, make sure all software and systems are updated regularly — attackers often exploit known weaknesses that patches would have already fixed.

featured.title: CrowdStrike says AI is now central to cyberattacks
featured.quote: AI-accelerated attacks now give defenders only 48 hours to patch vulnerabilities before exploitation.
